cohort: Participants were singleton births in the Wellington region between July and December 2019, excluding those domiciled outside Wellington, with HbA1c >=50mmol/mol, pre-existing diabetes, gestational diabetes, or an HbA1c not performed before 20 weeks gestation or taken at >=20 weeks.
finding: High normal early pregnancy HbA1c was not associated with a difference in birth weight or an increased risk of overall adverse perinatal outcomes in pregnant individuals without gestational diabetes, but was associated with significantly lower odds of post-partum haemorrhage and composite maternal adverse outcomes.
birth_weight: measured as an outcome for singleton births
